absent: Internals of range update, page queueing, page migration, migration target allocation and page return paths beyond caller side ordering.
Construction and validation inside policy creation, nodemask installation, policy duplication for ranges, and effective policy resolution for areas and files.
Task policy installation and query paths and whole address space migration beyond their call signatures.
Interleave selectors, weighted state table layout and update protocol, and single node plus mask resolution.
Area iteration, file offset mapping, page address lookup, folio helpers and zone list selection beyond observed usage.
Numeric values of policy modes, mode flag bits, move behavior bits, error codes and page size constants.
Authorization, capability, ptrace style access, security hook and cpuset allowed mask maintenance semantics.
Compat bitmap helpers and user copy primitives beyond success versus fault behavior.
Effect of the home node field on later allocation and migration decisions.
Reference counting and lifetime rules for shared interval policies beyond observed acquire and release pairing.

findings.text: The range bind interface accepts a start address with length plus mode, node bitmap pointer, bitmap size and move flags, normalizes the address tag, validates mode and flags, loads the user node set, then applies range policy with optional migration.

The task policy setter accepts a mode with embedded flag bits plus user bitmap and size, separates mode from flags with validation, loads the node set, then forwards the result to the task policy installer.

The policy query accepts optional user pointers for mode value and node bitmap plus size, target address and query flags, checks bitmap capacity against online node count, normalizes the address, obtains the effective policy and node set, then copies results back with zero extension.

The migration interface accepts a process identifier with bitmap size and two user bitmaps for source and destination sets, loads both sets into scratch masks, resolves the target task, checks access rights and allowed nodes, then invokes whole address space migration with privilege derived move scope.

The home node setter accepts a range with target node and reserved flags, requires page aligned start with zero flags and an online node, rounds length upward, then walks overlapping areas under exclusive address space lock updating only bind family areas.

Exposes a predicate reporting whether the effective policy for the start of a given area requests migration on fault, falling back to the caller task policy when the area carries none, releasing any temporary reference before returning.

Exposes a selector returning the preferred allocation node for slab use from the caller task policy, defaulting to the local node when called outside task context or without a policy, with per mode derivation for the supported policy kinds.

Exposes a membership test indicating whether a task belongs to an out of memory domain defined by a node mask, treating a null mask as universal membership and otherwise intersecting only bind policies under task lock.

Exposes a folio allocator for a given area and address that suppresses allocation warnings for droppable areas, resolves the effective policy and interleave position for the requested order, allocates through the policy aware path, then releases the policy reference.

Exposes a bulk page allocator that chooses the task policy outside interrupt context unless constrained to the local node, dispatching interleave family and preferred many to dedicated distributors and all other modes through a single node plus mask lookup.

Exposes a duplicator that allocates a new policy object, copies the source under task lock when the source is the caller task policy and otherwise by plain copy, rebinds against current allowed nodes when a cpuset rebound is in progress, then sets the reference count to one.
Exposes an equality test over policy objects covering mode, flags, home node, stored user masks and effective node masks with special handling for local mode.

Exposes lifecycle operations for file shared policies and task policy teardown: install or clear a range entry derived from area file offsets with cleanup on failure, drain every interval node when the tree is non empty, and detach plus drop the task policy under lock.

Range binding rejects unknown move flags, requires privilege for whole system move scope, requires page aligned start, clears strict checking for default mode, rounds length upward, rejects address wrap and treats an empty range as success before allocating any policy.

Mode sanitization splits embedded flag bits from the mode value, rejects out of range modes and mutually exclusive static versus relative node options, and permits balancing related flags only for bind family modes while expanding them into related fault behaviors.

User node set loading adjusts the size argument, treats empty size or null pointer as an empty set, rejects sizes beyond one page of bits, verifies that requested nodes beyond implementation support are all zero word by word from the end, then loads the in range portion with tail bits cleared.

Result bitmap export sizes the user transfer from the requested size rounded to wide units, truncates to the implemented node count with zero fill for the remainder while rejecting oversized requests beyond one page, then uses compat or native copy paths according to caller mode.

Home node update skips areas without a policy, fails when any area in range uses a mode outside the bind family without rolling back earlier updates, duplicates the old policy before mutating its home field under area write protection, then reinstalls the range.

Shared interval replacement removes entries fully covered by the new range, trims entries overlapping only one edge, splits an entry spanning the whole range by allocating a trailing remainder preserving the old policy, then inserts the new entry when present.
Two policies compare equal only when mode, flags and home node match, stored user masks match when the mode retains them, and node masks match for mask based modes, while local mode ignores masks.

Slab node choice returns the first set node for preferred, the rotating choice for interleave variants, the first usable zone node within the mask for the bind family with fallback to local when no zone qualifies, and the local node for local mode.

Bulk allocation outside interrupt context without a strict local constraint uses the caller task policy; interleave variants and preferred many each use a dedicated distributor, while remaining modes resolve a single node and optional mask before one bulk request.

Plain interleave bulk distribution divides the requested count evenly across set nodes, giving one extra page to leading nodes when the division has a remainder, advancing the rotating selector once per node and accumulating only pages actually obtained.

Weighted bulk distribution snapshots the allowed mask with retry on concurrent change, finishes any partially consumed weight on the previous node, loads per node weights with uniform fallback, then issues at most one bulk request per node using full rounds plus a leading delta while recording resume position.

Preferred many bulk allocation first attempts the full request restricted to the policy mask without direct reclaim, failure warnings or guaranteed success, then requests any shortfall without restriction on the local node with original reclaim behavior.

Process migration resolves a null identifier to the caller, fails unknown tasks, requires access authorization plus a security hook, requires the destination set to be within the target allowed set unless privileged, intersects the destination with the caller allowed set and stops when that intersection is empty.

Range binding holds the address space exclusively while installing the node mask and while queueing pages plus updating areas, ensuring concurrently inserted pages are not missed, and releases before blocking migration and on every path after acquisition.
Home node update holds the address space exclusively across the whole overlapping area walk and per area reinstall, releasing exactly once on completion or early failure.
Task policy pointers and bind mask membership are accessed under task lock for duplication, detachment and domain testing, with reference count handling performed after extracting the stable pointer.

The shared interval tree is mutated under an exclusive shared policy lock for replacement, insertion, deletion and full teardown, with allocation performed without the lock followed by restart when a split requires new nodes.

Task lookup for migration and weighted table sampling use read side critical sections, scratch node masks provide temporary storage for source, destination and validation masks with guaranteed release, and allowed mask snapshots retry when a concurrent change is detected.

The policy object carries a mode selector, behavior flags, an effective node mask, a home node identifier, a reference count, and for modes retaining user input a separate stored user mask; the fragments show mode dependent use of masks and home node.

The file shared state holds a lock plus a balanced tree root; each interval node holds file offset start and end, a pointer to its policy object, and a tree link, with ownership transferred to the tree on insertion and released through policy drop plus cache free on removal.

The bind migration context pairs a policy pointer with an interleave start index; for interleave families the index derives from the effective policy at the address of the first queued ordinary folio adjusted by folio position, otherwise it starts at zero.

Binding progresses through validation, policy creation, mask installation under lock, page queueing with a locked scan, area range update, lock release, synchronous migration of queued pages through a policy aware allocator, strict failure promotion, and return of queued pages plus policy release.

Replacement attempts mutation under lock, and when a spanning entry requires a remainder node that is not yet allocated it drops the lock, allocates node and policy objects, then restarts the scan from the beginning, releasing unused allocations on failure.

Migration progresses through scratch acquisition, source and destination mask loading, task resolution and privilege checks, allowed set filtering, security authorization, address space reference acquisition, whole space migration, and ordered release of task, memory and scratch resources.

Invalid addresses, sizes, modes, flags, nodes and offline home targets report invalid argument; insufficient privilege or disallowed node access report permission; allocation failures report out of memory; user copy faults report bad address; strict migration shortfalls report input output error; unsupported home modes report not supported; unknown tasks report no such process.

Cache influence is disabled before queueing plus migration when any move behavior is requested and re-enabled on exit; queued pages are returned when non empty; a non empty failure count combined with strict checking converts the final status to an error.

Bitmap transfers select compat or native helpers based on caller mode, mask unused tail bits in the final word, clear the excess tail region when the user request exceeds implemented size, and treat partial copy failures as user memory faults rather than partial success.

The fragments observe distinct policy selectors for default, bind, preferred, preferred many, interleave, weighted interleave and local, with default represented by a null policy object and local ignoring node masks.

The fragments observe mode flag bits for static versus relative nodes and balancing behavior, range move behavior bits for move, move all, strict and discontinuous tolerance plus internal inverted and write locked scan modifiers, and address alignment derived from the system page size.
